facts.statement: The genus Acrodus was described by Agassiz in Alberti in 1834.
Acrodus is an extinct genus of hybodont sharks named for its 'high' and 'tooth' characteristics.
facts.quote: Acrodus (from , 'high' and 'tooth') is an extinct genus of hybodont spanning from the Early Triassic to the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Acrodus was a durophagous shark with blunt, broad teeth adapted for crushing and grinding.
facts.quote: It was durophagous, with blunt, broad teeth designed for crushing and grinding.

facts.statement: Some Middle Triassic species of Acrodus are suggested to have reached lengths between 1.8 and 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: Some Middle Triassic species have been suggested to have grown to lengths of 1.8-2.5 m.

facts.statement: Acrodus species inhabited both marine and freshwater environments, though all Middle and Late Jurassic species are known only from freshwater.
facts.quote: Species are known from both marine and freshwater environments, with all Middle and Late Jurassic species only known from freshwater.

facts.statement: Acrodus is classified in the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Chondrichthyes, order Hybodontiformes, and family Acrodontidae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Chondrichthyes ordo: † Hybodontiformes familia: Acrodontidae genus: Acrodus

facts.statement: The genus Acrodus was named by Louis Agassiz in 1938.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado en 1938 por Louis Agassiz.

facts.statement: Acrodus lived from the Asselian to the Thanetian stages, spanning from 298.9 to 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Asselian to Thanetian (298.9 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 170 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus Acrodus.
